subject: biology-1
question: A single cell cannot grow without limit. Which physical constraint involving the **surface-area-to-volume ratio** sets the maximum size a cell can reach?

options.text: A very large cell would need more DNA than a single nucleus can hold.
A very large cell would have a cell wall too thick to absorb nutrients.
A very large cell could not divide its ribosomes fast enough.
Surface area grows more slowly than volume, so exchange across the membrane cannot keep up with the cell's needs.

explanation: As a cell grows, volume increases as the cube of its size while surface area increases only as the square, so beyond a limit the membrane cannot supply the cytoplasm fast enough. A fails because DNA content does not set the size limit. B fails because most cells have no wall at all. C fails because ribosome numbers grow along with the cell and are not the constraint.
